concepts.name: Target audience
concepts.summary: Recall that instruction is designed for a specific group of learners whose prior knowledge, context and motivation shape what will work.

concepts.name: Learning objectives
concepts.summary: Explain that a learning objective states what a learner will be able to do after instruction and why it guides every other design decision.

concepts.name: Content versus learning
concepts.summary: Understand that presenting information is not the same as ensuring learners can use it, and that design aims at the latter.

concepts.name: Instructional activities
concepts.summary: Describe how activities such as explanation, demonstration, practice and discussion give learners chances to engage with content.

concepts.name: Assessment purpose
concepts.summary: Understand that assessment gathers evidence of whether learners reached the objectives, rather than just assigning grades.

concepts.name: ADDIE phases
concepts.summary: Name the five ADDIE phases and state what each one is for in the design process.

misconceptions.text: Good instruction means covering all the content as thoroughly as possible.
Learning objectives describe what the instructor will teach.
Assessment happens only at the end to give a grade.

concepts.name: Bloom's taxonomy for objectives
concepts.summary: Classify objectives by cognitive level and pick verbs that match the intended depth of learning.

concepts.name: Writing measurable objectives
concepts.summary: Write objectives with an observable performance, conditions and criterion, using action verbs instead of vague ones like understand.

concepts.name: Basic needs analysis
concepts.summary: Use surveys, interviews and observation to identify the gap between current and desired performance and the audience's starting point.

concepts.name: Objective-assessment alignment
concepts.summary: Create assessment items that measure exactly the performance stated in an objective.

concepts.name: Content chunking and sequencing
concepts.summary: Break content into manageable units and order them logically, such as simple to complex or prerequisite first.

concepts.name: Formative and summative assessment
concepts.summary: Distinguish assessment used during learning to guide improvement from assessment used at the end to judge achievement.

concepts.name: Feedback to learners
concepts.summary: Provide timely, specific feedback on practice that tells learners what to do to improve.

misconceptions.text: Objectives that say learners will understand or appreciate a topic are measurable enough.
Higher Bloom levels are always better, so every objective should target creating or evaluating.
A needs assessment just means asking learners what they want to learn.

concepts.name: Task and content analysis
concepts.summary: Break a target performance into its component tasks, knowledge and skills to determine what must be taught.

concepts.name: Cognitive load management
concepts.summary: Apply principles like reducing extraneous load and managing element interactivity to material and activity design.

concepts.name: Practice and retrieval design
concepts.summary: Design practice that requires recall and application, distributed over time and with increasing difficulty.

concepts.name: Instructional strategy selection
concepts.summary: Analyse an objective and learner context to choose between strategies such as direct instruction, case study, simulation or collaborative work.

concepts.name: Gagné's events of instruction
concepts.summary: Structure a lesson using events such as gaining attention, stating objectives, presenting content, eliciting practice and giving feedback.

concepts.name: Rubrics and assessment validity
concepts.summary: Build rubrics and judge whether an assessment validly and reliably measures the intended objective.

concepts.name: Kirkpatrick evaluation levels
concepts.summary: Plan evaluation across reaction, learning, behavior and results and apply it to a program.

misconceptions.text: Learners have fixed learning styles, and teaching to each person's preferred style improves learning.
Adding more visuals, animation and audio always improves learning.
Positive learner satisfaction ratings show that the training worked.

concepts.name: Performance problem diagnosis
concepts.summary: Judge whether a performance gap stems from knowledge and skill, or from motivation, tools, incentives or environment, and decide if training is the right solution.

concepts.name: Instructional design models comparison
concepts.summary: Evaluate process models such as ADDIE, SAM and Dick and Carey and choose one based on project constraints and uncertainty.

concepts.name: Learning transfer design
concepts.summary: Design pre-, during- and post-training supports such as job aids, manager involvement and application tasks so skills transfer to work.

concepts.name: Modality and blended design
concepts.summary: Analyse trade-offs between delivery modes and combine them so each part of the objective is served by the best fit.

concepts.name: Motivation and engagement design
concepts.summary: Analyse sources of learner motivation and design attention, relevance, confidence and satisfaction supports accordingly.

concepts.name: Learning analytics and item analysis
concepts.summary: Interpret assessment and usage data to find weak items, content or activities and revise the design.

concepts.name: Accessibility and inclusive design
concepts.summary: Evaluate a design against accessibility and UDL principles and revise it to reduce barriers for diverse learners.

misconceptions.text: Training is the right answer to any performance problem.
Learners who pass the end-of-course test will automatically apply the skills at work.
Moving a face-to-face course online unchanged gives an equivalent learning experience.

concepts.name: Evidence-based design synthesis
concepts.summary: Critically evaluate research claims and weigh learning science evidence against context when making design decisions.

concepts.name: Complex skill design models
concepts.summary: Create learning programs for complex skills using whole-task sequences, scaffolding and fading of support.

concepts.name: Program-level evaluation strategy
concepts.summary: Design evaluation plans that isolate the training effect, link to business or organizational outcomes and inform decisions about continuing the program.

concepts.name: Adaptive and personalized pathways
concepts.summary: Create learning pathways that adapt content, pacing or support to learner diagnostics while preserving objective alignment.

concepts.name: Learning ecosystem architecture
concepts.summary: Design coherent curricula and ecosystems that combine formal training, performance support and social learning to meet organizational goals.

concepts.name: Design trade-off judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs among rigor, cost, time and stakeholder demands, and defend which design compromises are acceptable.

concepts.name: Stakeholder and SME leadership
concepts.summary: Evaluate and manage stakeholder expectations and subject matter expert input, including expert blind spots, to keep the design focused on outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Following a single proven model or framework rigorously guarantees an effective course.
ROI calculations can fully and cleanly prove the value of training.
Subject matter experts know best how the content should be taught.
